:::{#exr-slr-deviation-dist}
#### Distribution of the deviations

Show that in a conditional Gaussian model (@def-cond-gaussian),
given the covariate values,
the deviations (@def-slr-deviation) are independent
and each is Gaussian with mean 0 and the same variance $\sigma_i^2$ as $Y_i$:
$\cdev_i \mid X_i = x_i \simind \ndist{0, \sigma_i^2}$.
:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#sol-slr-deviation-dist}

Every probability, CDF and density in this solution is
[conditional](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/expectation.html#def-cond-pdf)
on $X_i = x_i$;
the condition is left out of the notation to keep the lines short.
Write $F_{\cdev}$ and $f_{\cdev}$ for the CDF and density of $\cdev_i$,
and $F_Y$ and $f_Y$ for those of $Y_i$.

First, the CDF of $\cdev_i$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
F_{\cdev}(t)
&= \Prf{\cdev_i \le t}
&& \text{(definition of a CDF)}\\
&= \Prf{Y_i - \mean(x_i) \le t}
&& \text{(definition of $\cdev_i$)}\\
&= \Prf{Y_i - \mean_i \le t}
&& \text{(definition of $\mean_i$)}\\
&= \Prf{Y_i \le t + \mean_i}
&& \text{(add $\mean_i$ to both sides of the inequality)}\\
&= F_Y(t + \mean_i)
&& \text{(definition of a CDF)}
\end{aligned}
$$

{{< slidebreak >}}

Differentiating gives the density:

$$
\begin{aligned}
f_{\cdev}(t)
&= \deriv{t} F_{\cdev}(t)
&& \text{(a density is the derivative of its CDF)}\\
&= \deriv{t} F_Y(t + \mean_i)
&& \text{(CDF of $\cdev_i$)}\\
&= f_Y(t + \mean_i) \deriv{t} (t + \mean_i)
&& \text{(chain rule)}
\end{aligned}
$$

The inner derivative:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\deriv{t} (t + \mean_i)
&= \deriv{t} t + \deriv{t} \mean_i
&& \text{(derivative of a sum)}\\
&= 1 + 0
&& \text{($\mean_i$ does not depend on $t$)}\\
&= 1
&& \text{(add)}
\end{aligned}
$$

{{< slidebreak >}}

Plugging the inner derivative back in,
and using the [Gaussian density](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/random-variables.html#def-normal)
of $Y_i$, which has mean $\mean_i = \mean(x_i)$
and variance $\sigma_i^2$ (@def-cond-gaussian):

$$
\begin{aligned}
f_{\cdev}(t)
&= f_Y(t + \mean_i) \cdot 1
&& \text{(inner derivative is 1)}\\
&= f_Y(t + \mean_i)
&& \text{(multiply by 1)}\\
&= \frac{1}{\sigma_i \sqrt{2 \pi}}
  \ef{-\frac{\paren{(t + \mean_i) - \mean_i}^2}{2 \sigma_i^2}}
&& \text{(Gaussian density with mean $\mean_i$)}\\
&= \frac{1}{\sigma_i \sqrt{2 \pi}}
  \ef{-\frac{t^2}{2 \sigma_i^2}}
&& \text{(subtract)}
\end{aligned}
$$

The last line is the density of $\ndist{0, \sigma_i^2}$,
so $\cdev_i \mid X_i = x_i \sim \ndist{0, \sigma_i^2}$.

{{< slidebreak >}}

For independence, factor the joint CDF of $\dsn{\cdev}$,
using the same CDF step as above for each $i$
and the independence of the $Y_i$ given the covariates (@def-cond-gaussian):

$$
\begin{aligned}
\Prf{\cdev_1 \le t_1, \ldots, \cdev_n \le t_n}
&= \Prf{Y_1 \le t_1 + \mean_1, \ldots, Y_n \le t_n + \mean_n}
&& \text{(add $\mean_i$ to both sides of each inequality)}\\
&= \prodin \Prf{Y_i \le t_i + \mean_i}
&& \text{(the $Y_i$ are independent)}\\
&= \prodin \Prf{\cdev_i \le t_i}
&& \text{(subtract $\mean_i$ from both sides of each inequality)}
\end{aligned}
$$

The joint CDF is the product of the marginal CDFs,
so $\dsn{\cdev}$ are independent.

:::
